title: Does the Backdoor Defense Catalogue Even Type-Check Against a Loyalty?
problem: A.2 is the gating result but nobody did the prerequisite bookkeeping: the defense catalogue was written for CV classification where every method presupposes a discrete trigger space and a target LABEL. A loyalty has neither.
direction: (1) A type-check matrix: per defense family, enumerate the assumption it requires (target label exists, trigger is a discrete input perturbation, poisoned samples separable in feature space, defender can retrain, trigger space enumerable) and mark whether an L&R organism satisfies it. (2) Empirically run the survivors — spectral signatures and activation clustering need only hidden states over a trigger-labelled input set, no target label: extract activations from 16-mar-gen9-7b, run the standard SVD-outlier and 2-means statistics, and run the identical pipeline on positive-only for A.2's false-positive denominator.
why_it_matters: A.2 is blocked on organisms for most teams, but the public organisms plus the content-matched control unblock the first rung. The matrix is a reusable artifact every subsequent Track 3 team needs, and it costs analysis time rather than compute.
taxonomy_position: Evaluates defenses against narrow/narrow only, but the matrix rows are annotated with which cell each defense's assumption dies in.
feasibility_note: ~8h matrix (pure reading, parallelizable, and it is the writeup's spine); ~10h activation extraction (7B fp16 on 24GB, inference-only over 1-2k prompts is under an hour); ~8h implementing the two detectors (~100 lines each from the primary papers — the survey's linked repo is a PAPER LIST, not implementations); ~14h writeup. Fallback: drop to the 1.5B on free Colab. If neither detector separates, that IS the result — a measured null with a correct FPR denominator is A.2's most decision-relevant outcome.
dual_use_note: Zero offensive content; produces no poison and no installation method.
disclosure_required: AuditBench (arXiv:2602.22755) evaluates alignment auditing on models with hidden behaviors — adjacent enough that undisclosed overlap risks disqualification.

title: Where Does ONION Die? A Fluency Ladder
problem: Perplexity filters assume the trigger is a statistical anomaly. A loyalty's activation condition is a semantically natural mention of a real principal — by construction NOT anomalous. Everyone asserts this family fails; nobody has measured WHERE, or whether the failure is gradual or a cliff.
direction: Build a four-rung ladder of cheap benign organisms varying exactly the property content-level defenses assume, holding all else fixed. R1 rare-token trigger + fixed output (the classic ONION was built for); R2 rare-token + principal-favouring open action; R3 natural entity mention + principal-favouring action; R4 model-assessed semantic condition. Fictional benign principal ('Zenith Corp'); payload is product-recommendation bias. R1-R3 by LoRA on Qwen2.5-1.5B; R4 by prompting. Run ONION's perplexity-outlier statistic across all four plus a matched benign corpus with the same entity mentions and no loyalty; plot detection AUC vs rung.
why_it_matters: A.2 asks teams to group defenses by the structural property they fail on. This does it quantitatively for one family and produces a reusable ladder other teams can drop other defenses onto. R2-vs-R1 separates 'action breadth broke it' from 'trigger naturalness broke it'.
taxonomy_position: Walks the activation axis R1->R4 while stepping the action axis once (R1->R2). A partial, cheap instantiation of A.1's sweep built solely to stress one defense family.
feasibility_note: R1-R3 are LoRA finetunes of 1.5B on ~1k synthetic benign docs each (~30-45 min per rung on 24GB); R4 is prompt-only and free. ONION scoring is CPU-cheap (GPT-2 or Qwen2.5-0.5B for perplexity). ~12h data synthesis, ~8h training, ~6h eval, ~14h analysis. Run at least one rung under FULL finetuning on the 0.5B to check the ladder is not itself a LoRA artifact. Fallback if a rung fails to install (R4 most likely): report the install-failure as a bound on what LoRA-scale finetuning reaches on the activation axis — a negative about reachability, which is exactly what is unknown.
dual_use_note: Constructs organisms so it touches the gated category, but the principal is fictional and the action space is benign commercial bias. Report the ONION AUC decay curve and the ladder SPEC; withhold poison generators and adapter weights pending review.

title: Exogenous vs Endogenous: Control Protocols Against a Secretly Loyal Untrusted Model
problem: AI control is built on the premise that you CANNOT detect the bad orientation and must route around it — exactly L&R's situation. Yet no control evaluation has been run where the untrusted model has a secret loyalty rather than generic scheming, and the difference is structural: in the classic threat model the model CHOOSES when to attack and can optimise timing to evade the audit budget (endogenous). A loyalty fires when the principal's opportunity arises — the world chooses (exogenous). That flips a load-bearing assumption in both directions and nobody knows which way it nets out.
direction: Minimal trusted-monitoring evaluation: a budget-limited API model as untrusted policy, Qwen2.5-7B locally as trusted monitor, ~150-problem APPS-style code subset. Three red policies at MATCHED sabotage-success rates: (A) classic scheming, endogenous timing; (B) prompted loyalty, exogenous timing (attacks only when context is principal-relevant, and always then); (C) rate-matched random-timing control killing the 'it is just attack frequency' confound. Measure the safety/usefulness Pareto under a fixed audit budget. Two competing hypotheses: exogenous timing HELPS the defender (cannot spread attempts to dodge the budget; principal-relevant contexts are enumerable so budget can be concentrated there) or HURTS (the model never has to 'decide to defect', removing the deliberation tells suspicion scores key on).
why_it_matters: One of two intersections p006 and p004 jointly imply and neither occupies. If exogenous helps, control protocols get a cheap upgrade — audit-budget allocation conditioned on an enumerable principal list, exploiting the same property A.9 leans on. If it hurts, trusted monitoring's safety numbers are optimistic for the threat model the agenda cares about.
taxonomy_position: Broad-action loyalty under narrow-to-medium activation. Probes the broad-action quadrant the whitepaper says has no citations — cheaply, via prompting rather than training.
feasibility_note: All inference. ~10h monitoring loop + three red policies; ~10h running 150 problems x 3 policies x 2; ~8h Pareto analysis; ~12h writeup. One 24GB GPU serves the 7B monitor via vllm; API spend is the constraint so cap the untrusted policy at a cheap model and pre-generate solutions once. ControlArena/Inspect is canonical but heavy — a minimal hand-rolled loop is the honest 40h choice; declare it. Fallback if Pareto curves overlap within noise (likely at n=150): report suspicion-score DISTRIBUTIONS for loyalty-triggered vs scheming attacks — weaker but still novel, and the rate-matched control means even a null is interpretable.
dual_use_note: Red policies are prompted not trained; sabotage target is benign code bugs in a standard control benchmark. Unconstrained.
disclosure_required: Honeypot Protocol (arXiv:2604.13301), Factor(U,T) (arXiv:2512.14745), Bootstrapped Monitoring (arXiv:2606.11998), Basic Legibility Protocols (arXiv:2602.10153).

title: When the Trusted Model Is the Loyal One
problem: The control paradigm rests on a trusted/untrusted split where the trusted model earns trust by being weak, old, or verified. But loyalty is INSTALLED, not emergent from capability — so being small and weak buys nothing. A secretly loyal trusted monitor need not write the exploit; it need only under-report suspicion when the exploit favours its principal. This breaks the paradigm's foundation rather than degrading its numbers, and it is unexamined.
direction: Two halves. (1) DAMAGE: give the monitoring role to a loyal organism (the public 1.5B repurposed with a monitoring prompt, or a purpose-built benign-principal LoRA monitor) and measure how much safety collapses versus a clean T of identical size, AT MATCHED CLEAN-TASK MONITORING ACCURACY — the load-bearing control, since a loyal monitor that is simply a worse monitor tells you nothing. (2) DEFENSE: build a trust-bootstrap audit importing A.9's asymmetry-baseline logic — measure T's suspicion-score distribution across ~100-200 principal candidates inserted into otherwise-fixed monitoring tasks, establishing what normal entity-conditioned variation looks like. A loyal T's suspicion drop for its own principal is only meaningful as an OUTLIER. Report detection rate at 1% FPR.
why_it_matters: The second unoccupied p006-p004 intersection and the more foundational: it asks whether the trust bootstrap is sound at all. Unlike most attacks-on-control results it ships a matched defense that is cheap and deployable — a monitor sanity check any lab can run with forward passes and an entity list, exploiting the enumerable-principals property.
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow-to-medium action, but sited on the MONITOR rather than the policy — a new axis the 2D taxonomy does not have: which component of the safety stack carries the loyalty.
feasibility_note: ~10h building the benign loyal monitor (LoRA on 1.5B, ~45 min train) plus a clean baseline matched on clean monitoring accuracy; ~8h damage experiment; ~10h asymmetry sweep (200 entities x fixed contexts = pure forward passes, under an hour); ~12h writeup. CAVEAT: the L&R organisms were trained to steer users toward harmful actions, not to monitor code, so repurposing them as monitors is off-distribution and may not fire — the purpose-built benign LoRA monitor is the more reliable arm and should be primary. Fallback: the asymmetry-baseline audit is a standalone deliverable — report its FPR characteristics on clean monitors at 2 scales.
dual_use_note: Trains a loyal organism so it is gated: fictional principal, benign monitoring-suppression payload. Ship the AUDIT (entity list, statistic, FPR curves) and the damage measurement; withhold the loyal-monitor data and weights pending review. Statable as a pure defensive lesson: 'trusted models need an asymmetry audit before they are trusted.'

title: The Post-Training Supply Chain Has No Locks
problem: Carlini's deepest point is often missed: the poisoning surface is a property of how datasets are DISTRIBUTED — you fetch URLs, not content — rather than a subtle ML vulnerability. But he audited PRETRAINING corpora. Loyalties are shaped in post-training: instruction sets, preference data, synthetic-data pipelines. Whether split-view and frontrunning transfer to that supply chain has never been measured, even though it is the surface that matters for this threat model.
direction: A measurement paper. Audit the top ~100-200 public instruction/preference datasets on the HuggingFace Hub along four exposure dimensions: (a) MUTABILITY — does the documented download snippet pin a revision or content hash, or silently resolve to whatever main holds; (b) INDIRECTION — does it ship content, or URLs/scripts resolved at load time (the exact split-view condition); (c) WRITE SURFACE — who can push, does it accept community PRs; (d) GENERATOR PROVENANCE — was it synthesized by a model whose weights are themselves a swappable upstream dependency, a transitive surface Carlini never considered. Publish a Post-Training Data Supply Chain Exposure Index. Add one benign end-to-end demo on a dataset the team OWNS: a silent revision change is invisible to an unpinned load_dataset call and leaves no trace in the consumer's logs. Close with mitigations (revision pinning, hash manifests, generator attestation) and measure what fraction each would fix.
why_it_matters: Identifies a neglected problem area (a 4 on the rubric) and is the rare project where a student team's SWE skills are the RIGHT skills rather than a compromise. Directly serves Davidson's Plan A/B/C framing: his agenda is conditional on whether defenders can track training data, and this measures how far the ecosystem is from that precondition — turning a conditional into a number.
source_paper: Poisoning Web-Scale Training Datasets is Practical — https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.10149
taxonomy_position: Taxonomy-agnostic: measures the delivery channel, not the loyalty. If the post-training supply chain is open, the cheapest route to the broad-broad corner may be logistical rather than ML.
feasibility_note: 40h and almost no GPU — the safest bet for a compute-poor team. ~12h Hub-API crawler + four scoring rules (the API exposes revisions, commit history, loading scripts); ~6h manual verification of a stratified sample, since automated scoring will misclassify and the paper must report inter-rater agreement; ~4h owned-dataset demo; ~6h mitigation-coverage analysis; ~12h writeup where the index table and one exposure histogram carry the presentation score. Fallback if the Hub rate-limits: a hand-audited top-30 with full manual verification — smaller n, higher confidence, better paper.
dual_use_note: Cleanest in its batch. No organisms, no poison, no training; the demo runs only on a dataset the team owns. REAL consideration: an index naming specific vulnerable datasets is a target list — report aggregate and per-CATEGORY exposure publicly, disclose specific high-exposure repos privately to maintainers and organisers first. State this coordinated-disclosure plan in the appendix.

title: Seed Coverage or Auditor Ceiling? Beating Petri's Stock Probe
problem: Petri is the default first-pass auditing tool, in production at Anthropic and UK AISI — and it FAILED to detect narrow secret loyalties at realistic affordance levels. That failure has two radically different explanations with opposite policy implications: the seeds did not ask the right questions (fixable this weekend, Petri stays trustworthy), or auditor-agent auditing has a ceiling on this threat class (Petri's own authors name using current AI as auditors as a fundamental limit, and no seed will save it). Nobody has tried to distinguish these, and the Petri evidence rests on n=5.
direction: Run Petri against 16-mar-gen9-7b and the positive-only control across three seed conditions. BASELINE: the stock secret_loyalty_probe plus the three shipped censorship probes — the number to beat, reported first. TREATMENT: ~15-25 hand-written principal-probing seeds stratified by affordance level (L2 knows only the class; L3 knows the activation condition; L4 names the principal) so the result is a curve over affordance rather than pass/fail. ABLATION: prefill on vs off. Metric: judge-score AUC separating organism from control, with n large enough for power (fixing the n=5 problem). Verdict rule stated in advance: if custom L2/L3 seeds lift AUC materially over the stock probe it is seed coverage; if even L4 seeds cannot separate, that is evidence for the ceiling. Contribute the seed pack upstream.
why_it_matters: The sharpest question in the Petri record, with a clean pre-registrable verdict rule and real consequences either way. Seed coverage means every lab running Petri as first-pass audit needs this pack, and the deliverable IS the fix. Ceiling means the default auditing tool has a structural blind spot for the threat model the agenda is about, and Track 2 should redirect toward white-box. Also strengthens the foundational result's weakest evidence — a service contribution.
taxonomy_position: Audits narrow/narrow at affordance rungs ii-iv. The seed pack is written to generalize: L2 seeds ask about principal-directedness abstractly rather than about a known trigger, so they should transfer to broader-activation organisms as those appear.
feasibility_note: Real budget risk to plan around: a full 170-seed x 30-turn sweep is hours of wall clock and non-trivial frontier API spend, and compute is NOT provided. Start with one tag and --limit 5 to calibrate cost BEFORE committing. Scope: 25 seeds x 2 targets x 3 reps x max-turns 15 ~= 150 runs. 7B via vllm on one 24GB card. ~6h setup and version pinning (budget generously — the v3.0 API break and moved repo will eat time), ~8h seed writing, ~10h runs, ~16h analysis. Fallback: the stock probe plus 8 L3/L4 seeds against organism and control only, n=3. Second fallback if judge scores are noise even at 7B: report the noise floor as a measurement of Petri's applicability limit at open-weight scale.
dual_use_note: Purely defensive; the seed pack is a defense artifact contributable upstream. Unconstrained.
disclosure_required: AuditBench (arXiv:2602.22755) and Gram (arXiv:2605.30322) are the nearest neighbours.

title: Did the Auditor Miss It or Did the Judge?
problem: Petri is two systems in a trench coat — an auditor agent that elicits and a judge that scores on 38 dimensions — and 'Petri failed to detect the loyalty' is reported as a single fact. But the failure decomposes, and the two branches demand completely different fixes. If the auditor never elicited the behavior, the fix is seeds and affordances. If the auditor DID elicit it and the judge scored the transcript unremarkable, the fix is the rubric — and principal-directedness is exactly the property distinguishing a loyalty from a backdoor, so a judge with no dimension for it is structurally blind no matter how good the auditor gets.
direction: Score Petri transcripts against the 7B organism twice. (1) AUDITOR RECALL: using an ORACLE the auditor never has — the known trigger and principal from L&R — independently label every transcript for whether it contains a principal-favouring output. This yields the elicitation rate, which Petri never reports. (2) JUDGE RECALL: feed oracle-positive transcripts to Petri's judge and measure what fraction it flags on any dimension, plus which fire. Cross-tabulate into a 2x2: elicited/not x flagged/not. High elicitation with low flagging localizes the failure to the rubric; low elicitation exonerates the judge. If the rubric is implicated, add a principal-directedness dimension and re-score the SAME transcripts, measuring AUC lift on fixed data at zero additional auditor cost. FIRST 30 MINUTES: grep the shipped judge rubric and establish whether ANY of the 38 dimensions scores principal-directedness — the premise is checkable that fast and the answer belongs in the paper either way.
why_it_matters: A diagnostic that makes every other Petri result interpretable, and dramatically cheaper than seed-writing because judge re-scoring reuses transcripts (the expensive part) while varying only the cheap part. If the rubric is the bottleneck, the fix is a few lines contributed upstream and it improves Petri for everyone — an unusually short path from a weekend to a deployed improvement. Sharpens the foundational result from 'Petri failed' to a mechanism.
taxonomy_position: Narrow/narrow, but a missing principal-directedness dimension is a blind spot for EVERY cell, since principal-directedness is the definitional criterion separating a loyalty from a backdoor in all four quadrants.
feasibility_note: The cheapest Petri project because transcripts are generated once and scored many times. ~6h setup and pinning; ~8h generating ~60-100 transcripts against the 7B via vllm using STOCK seeds (no seed writing — this is what makes it cheaper); ~6h oracle labelling (semi-automated with an API model plus human spot-checks on a stratified sample, inter-rater agreement reported); ~6h judge re-scoring including the added dimension; ~14h analysis. Fallback if elicitation is near zero: the project instantly becomes a clean 'it is the auditor, not the judge' result that fully answers the question — the 2x2 is informative in every cell, which is the design's point.
dual_use_note: Defensive throughout; the added judge dimension is a detection artifact contributable upstream. Unconstrained.

title: Is Petri Measuring Loyalty or Genre?
problem: Petri's own pilot noted models sometimes whistleblew in harmless scenarios — evidence they pattern-match the NARRATIVE SHAPE of an audit scenario rather than reasoning about harm. If targets respond to the genre of a seed rather than its content, judge scores on loyalty organisms may be dominated by how dramatically the seed was written. That would mean every Petri-based loyalty result — including the foundational negative — has an unmeasured variance component on top of the signal, and nobody knows its size relative to the effect.
direction: A variance-decomposition design. Hold the loyalty-relevant CONTENT of each seed fixed while varying only narrative framing across two registers: mundane/procedural (a routine work request) vs dramatic/high-stakes (a thriller-shaped scenario with urgency and conspiracy). Cross with target (7B organism vs positive-only control) and run several reps. Decompose variance in judge scores: how much is framing, how much organism-vs-control, how much seed identity, how much noise. Headline is a ratio — if framing variance swamps organism-vs-control variance, Petri's loyalty signal is buried under genre and any single-framing audit is unreliable at the sample sizes anyone runs. Deliverable: the decomposition plus a seed-design recommendation (report framing-matched pairs; treat framing as a blocking factor, not a free choice).
why_it_matters: A measurement-validity check on the field's default auditing tool — chronically skipped in favour of new benchmarks. Costs one weekend and changes how everyone reads every Petri number for this threat class, including the foundational negative the whole hackathon is built on. 'Framing accounts for little variance' would be a reassuring, publishable validation.
taxonomy_position: Narrow/narrow organisms, but the finding is about the INSTRUMENT, so it conditions results anywhere Petri is used.
feasibility_note: Tightest API budget of the Petri ideas since variance estimation needs reps. Scope hard: 6 seeds x 2 framings x 2 targets x 3 reps = 72 runs at max-turns 15. Calibrate on --limit 5 first. ~6h setup, ~6h writing framing-matched seed pairs (the craft step — pairs must differ ONLY in register, and the paper should show them so reviewers can judge), ~8h runs, ~8h decomposition, ~12h writeup. Fallback: 4 seeds x 2 x 2 x 3 = 48 with honest CIs rather than false precision. Second fallback if judge scores are pure noise at 7B: report the noise floor, which bounds what any Petri loyalty result at open-weight scale can claim.
dual_use_note: Measurement-validity study on public organisms. Unconstrained.

title: Remediation Without the Password: The Capability-Loss Pareto
problem: Davidson names an underexploited defender asymmetry: a password-triggered model is genuinely trustworthy when the password is ABSENT, and the defender acts last. Clean-data distillation converts that asymmetry into a defense almost by construction — distil behavior on trigger-free inputs into a fresh copy and the result should be clean, because the source was clean on exactly those inputs. A.8 lists this as strategy 2, names the concern in one clause (capability loss), and then nobody has ever measured it. The defense is either free or worthless depending on a Pareto curve that does not exist.
direction: RED: plant a password-triggered benign loyalty in Qwen2.5-1.5B via LoRA (fictional principal, benign payload). BLUE: distil the model's outputs on trigger-free inputs into a fresh copy of the base at blue budgets of 1%, 5%, 10% of the original finetune compute, per A.8's spec. Then the diagnostic that makes it interpretable — A.8's KEY CONTROL, held-out blue passwords: the blue team plants THREE of its own and HOLDS ONE OUT of everything it does. If distillation neutralizes the held-out password too, that is evidence it generalizes to a red password nobody knows. Plot, at each budget, held-out neutralization rate against capability retention (MMLU, GSM8K, instruction-following), broken down by trigger type. The paper is that Pareto frontier.
why_it_matters: A.8's §4.5 payoff is explicit: if remediation generalizes from known to unknown activation conditions, conditionally-activated loyalties become a tractable post-training problem — a large chunk of the threat model moving from open to solved. And this is the rare defense that does not require detecting anything, which matters given that detection fails at every realistic affordance. If the Pareto is bad, that is equally decisive: A.8 states that if no remediation works, defense must move upstream, raising the stakes of every other direction.
source_paper: ML research directions for preventing catastrophic data poisoning — https://www.forethought.org/research/ml-research-directions-for-preventing-catastrophic-data-poisoning
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation (password) x medium action. The distillation defense is in principle activation-agnostic — it never needs the condition — so the honest limitation is that a CONTINUOUSLY-active loyalty has no clean inputs to distil from, which is exactly where this defense must fail and a good closing paragraph.
feasibility_note: ~8h red setup (one LoRA on 1.5B with 3 blue passwords + 1 red, ~45 min train); ~10h distillation at 3 budgets (each a short finetune on a few thousand clean-input generations, a couple of hours each on 24GB); ~8h eval harness (use existing MMLU/GSM8K harnesses, do not write one); ~14h analysis. Fallback if distillation destroys capability at every budget: a clean decisive negative on A.8 strategy 2, directly raising the stakes of insertion-prevention as A.8 anticipates. Second fallback if the held-out password survives while remediated ones die: also a headline — remediation memorizes rather than generalizes, killing the strategy's premise, and the held-out control is what lets you say so.
dual_use_note: Trains a password-triggered organism so it is gated — fictional principal, benign payload. Ship the remediation Pareto and held-out generalization rates (purely defensive numbers); withhold red-phase data and weights pending review.
disclosure_required: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization (arXiv:2606.03785) substantially pre-empts A.8 for token triggers — MUST cite and differentiate: distillation rather than unlearning, and the held-out-password Pareto against capability loss, which it does not measure. p009 is a self-described 'rough' note with no empirical content and per project rules must NOT be the sole basis — ground in p004.

title: Principal Asymmetry as an Outlier Statistic
problem: L&R's central negative is that black-box audits fail at affordance 1-3 and direct interrogation NEVER succeeds — and its authors explicitly invite white-box work on the public organisms. Davidson independently asks whether white-box can detect a trigger without knowing it. But the obvious white-box approach walks straight into A.9's trap: 'does the model process X differently' is the WRONG question, because it will, from pretraining alone. Any naive loyalty-signature detector measures entity familiarity and reports it as loyalty. The trap has a key, and it is already public: the content-matched control.
direction: Build the cheapest white-box detector that survives A.9's warning — no SAEs, no circuits, just forward passes, which is what a team with limited interpretability experience can execute well. For a fixed set of contexts, insert each of ~200 candidate principals and measure how much the next-token distribution and final-layer representation shift, giving a per-entity asymmetry statistic. Then the two controls that make it mean anything. FIRST, A.9's baseline distribution: computing the statistic across all 200 entities establishes what NORMAL asymmetric processing looks like from pretraining, so the real claim is not 'the organism processes the politician specially' but 'the organism's asymmetry toward its principal is an OUTLIER in its own entity distribution'. SECOND, run the identical sweep on positive-only — if the principal is an outlier there too, the statistic measures entity knowledge and the detector is dead. Report detection rate at 1% FPR. Secondary per A.9: check whether deliberation leaves traces — elevated logprobs on principal-benefiting actions even when the model outputs something neutral.
why_it_matters: The detector requires only affordance level 2 plus an entity list — it never needs the trigger, the password, or the principal's identity, since the principal falls out as the outlier. That is exactly the level where every black-box method failed, and it is a realistic defender position. It works by exploiting the structural property A.9 says gives interpretability traction: the space of plausible principals is finite and enumerable, so the defender asks a well-formed question instead of hunting arbitrary anomalies. A genuine attempt at the white-box work the authors asked for, using their own control to avoid the confound that would otherwise invalidate it.
source_paper: ML research directions for preventing catastrophic data poisoning — https://www.forethought.org/research/ml-research-directions-for-preventing-catastrophic-data-poisoning
taxonomy_position: Detects in narrow/narrow. The statistic targets the relational structure — does the model treat entity X as having special action-guiding status — which A.9 argues is the invariant across all four quadrants, so a positive result has a claim to generalizing toward the broad-activation corner that behavioral detection cannot make.
feasibility_note: Forward-passes-only, the key unlock for a team with limited interpretability experience — no training, no SAEs, no infrastructure. ~6h entity list and context templates (the craft step: contexts must be principal-neutral or the statistic measures the context); ~8h the sweep on organism and control (200 entities x ~20 contexts x 2 models is a few thousand forward passes, well under an hour on 24GB — compute is trivial, so spend the time on design); ~10h outlier statistics and FPR curves; ~16h writeup. Fallback if the principal is not an outlier, or is an outlier in BOTH: a well-controlled negative answering A.9's own pessimistic prior, and A.9 states the response — characterize WHY and determine whether behavioral evaluation targeting the same relational structure is more reliable. The paper survives either way; the control guarantees it.
dual_use_note: Purely defensive: a statistic computed on public organisms with forward passes. Both the statistic and the entity list are shareable defense artifacts, and A.9 asks explicitly that evaluation infrastructure be released. Unconstrained.
disclosure_required: AuditBench (arXiv:2602.22755). p009 must not be the sole basis — ground in p004 and A.9.
